div.head: VI As 6.4
div.ab: ⁊ þæt ceapgild aríse a ofer XXX pæng̅ oð healf pund, syððan we hit æscað, furðor, gif we þæt ceapgild arærað be fullan angylde; ⁊ beo sy æsce forð, swa hit ær gecweden wæs, þeah heo læsse sy.

Et ceapgildum exurgat semper super XXX den. ad X sol.; postea demandabimus hoc in antea, si ceapgildum illud eleuemus pleno angildo; et sit inquisitio procedens, sicut ante dictum (predictum) est, quamuis etiam minor sit.
⁊ þæt ceapgild aríse á ofer XXX pæn̄g oð healf pund, syððan we hit æscað, furðor, gif we þæt ceapgild arærað be fullan angylde; ⁊ beo sy æsce forð, swa hit ær gecweden wæs, þeah heo læsse sy.

Und das [uns zukommende] Ersatzgeld, sobald wir [den Dieb gerichtlich nachweisen und] es einklagen, steige jedesmal über [mindestens] 30 Pfennig bis zu einem halben Pfund [und] ferner hinauf, wenn wir den Ersatz zu vollem Werthe [eines theureren Sklaven, nicht bloss zur Taxe] erheben; es trete jedoch die Nachforschung, so wie es vorher bestimmt worden ist, auch dann ein, wenn sie weniger [als 30 Pfennig uns eintragen] wird.

And the compensation-money [due to us], as soon as we [legally trace the thief and] sue for it, is in every case to rise above [at least] 30 pence up to half a pound [and] further still, if we raise the compensation at the full value [of a dearer slave, not just at the fixed rate]; the search is nevertheless to take place, as was determined before, even if it will [bring us] less [than 30 pence].

When the value of the goods is more than thirty pence, the sum to be paid shall never be less than half a pound, when we have instituted a search. It shall rise to a larger amount, if we succeed in obtaining payment to the full value of the goods. But a search must be continued, as has already been declared, even when the amount involved is less [than thirty pence].

And the price [paid in compensation] for goods worth over 30 pence is always to mount as far as half a pound, after we search for it, further, if we obtain compensation at the full value; and the search is to go on, as was agreed before, although it [the sum involved] is less.

Q scheint denselben Text wie wir gelesen, aber nicht verstanden zu haben. Schmid verwirft die früheren Übersetzungen richtig als unklar. Er nimmt ceapgild als die Summe, welche die Gilde von allen [besser: vielen] Genossen einfordert behufs Erstattung des Gestohlenen an den Einzelnen. Allein wie konnte diese Beitragssumme je nur 30 Pf. betragen, da doch ½ Pf. von jedem Genossen schon viel mehr ergab? Und wurden denn für Ersetzung eines Schafes 4 Pf. besonders gesammelt? Wir hören doch von Sammlung erst da, wo es galt, 120 Pf. aufzubringen. — Ich verstehe ceapgild aræran wie gild aræran 6, 3: ‘vor Gericht Geldanspruch auf Ersatz des Gestohlenen durchsetzen’

Q seems to have read the same text as we have, but not to have understood it. Schmid rightly rejects the earlier translations as unclear. He takes ceapgild as the sum that the gild demands from all [better: many] members for the purpose of reimbursing the individual for what was stolen. But how could this contribution ever amount to only 30 pence, since ½ penny from each member already produced much more? And were 4 pence specially collected for the replacement of a sheep? After all, we hear of a collection only where 120 pence had to be raised. — I understand ceapgild aræran like gild aræran 6, 3: ‘to enforce in court a money claim for compensation for what was stolen’

‘after we make search’ bei Price-Thorpe tadelt Schmid als unklar. Er denkt als Zahler die Gilde, als Empfänger den Bestohlenen, und trennt [!] dies æscan von æsce 2 Zeilen weiter. Ich beziehe beides auf die Verfolgung der Gilde gegen den Dieb. — In Q kann das Gallolatein. demandare ‘fordern’ sowohl ‘gerichtlich einklagen’ wie ‘als Beisteuer einziehen’ bedeuten. Ich verstehe, die Gilde erhalte von gewonnenem Diebstahlsprozess, auch wenn nur 1 Schaf eingeklagt war, mindestens 30 Pf. Justizertrag

Schmid criticises ‘after we make search’ in Price-Thorpe as unclear. He takes the gild as payer, the man robbed as recipient, and separates [!] this æscan from æsce 2 lines further on. I refer both to the gild’s prosecution of the thief. — In Q the Gallo-Latin demandare ‘demand’ can mean both ‘sue for in court’ and ‘collect as a contribution’. I understand that the gild received at least 30 pence in judicial proceeds from a successful theft suit, even if only 1 sheep had been sued for
Q irrt wie o. 6, 1⁴
Q errs as above 6, 1⁴
Archetyp interpungierte nicht; daher zog Q furðor zum vorigen Satz und verstand ‘künftig’
The archetype had no punctuation; hence Q took furðor with the preceding sentence and understood ‘in future’

‘wenn der Wert der gestohlenen Sache über die gesetzliche Schätzung ansteigt’ Schmid 531a richtig; so Schreuer Verbrechenskonk. 42 gegen K. Maurer, der in angild Busse ausser ceapgield erblickte. Ich verstehe nicht Toller 43: ‘if we raise the market price to the full fixed price’

‘if the value of the stolen object rises above the legal valuation’ Schmid 531a rightly; so Schreuer Verbrechenskonk. 42 against K. Maurer, who saw in angild a compensation besides the ceapgield. I do not understand Toller 43: ‘if we raise the market price to the full fixed price’
[Setze diese Zahl zu ‘Sklaven’.] Unter einzelnen Stücken Vieh galt nur der Sklav über ½ £
[Attach this number to ‘slaves’.] Among individual head of livestock only the slave was worth more than ½ £

‘Die Nachsuchung’ Schmid richtig. — Der Dieb soll jedenfalls bestraft werden, auch wenn die Gilde wegen Versäumnis der Meldefrist kein Versicherungsgeld zu zahlen braucht (8 8), und obwohl es der Gilde — wegen Armut des Diebes — wenig oder nichts einbringt. — Price will hit, auf ceapgield bezogen, emendieren: ohne Grund

‘The search’ Schmid rightly. — The thief is to be punished in any case, even if the gild need pay no insurance money because the time-limit for reporting has been missed (8 8), and although it brings the gild — because of the thief’s poverty — little or nothing. — Price would emend hit, referring it to ceapgield: without reason

Liebermann interprets this differently. He understands ofer xxx pæñg as the minimum to be paid by the convicted thief and translates the first clause: ‘Und das [uns zukommende] Ersatzgeld, sobald wir [den Dieb gerichtlich nachweisen und] es einklagen, steige jedesmal über [mindestens] 30 Pfennig bis zu einem halben Pfund und ferner hinauf etc.’ But ought not ofer xxx pæñg to be interpreted like ofer xii pæningas in cap. 1 § 1, above, and ‘half a pound’ to be taken as the minimum payment to be made by the thief? The clause furðor gif we etc. seems to contain an ellipsis—‘when the value of the goods stolen exceeds half a pound etc.’
This clause, gif we þæt…angylde, seems to imply that the thief may not be able to pay to the full value of the goods.
A literal translation of the clause þeah heo læsse sy would be ‘though it is a smaller one,’ it (heo) referring to æsce (search).
